initial_query: I use separate --with-x and --without-x flags that control the same setting. With the enabling flag configured as the default, --without-x unexpectedly leaves the setting enabled. Please make explicit flags work, preserving no-argument behavior and the order of repeated flags.
failure_symptom: `--without-x` yields the default enabled value; no-argument and `--with-x` may still pass.
expected_sop: List possible sources including explicit-default metadata → check tie-break after parsing → test all flag combinations.

feedback_by_state.primary: Using --without-x still leaves the setting enabled.
feedback_by_state.edge: Repeated flags or the alternative default configuration still return the wrong setting.
feedback_by_state.exception: The reported origin does not match the value explicitly supplied on the command line.
feedback_by_state.regression: The no-argument default or a normal slash-paired flag has changed.

success_condition: All subgraders pass; infrastructure errors never count as PASS.
review_reason: Adjusted after real validation: adding a default winner in handle_parse_result did NOT break the task because shared-destination options both consume the same CLI source. Use Option.consume_value to replace explicit False with its explicit default while retaining source metadata; downstream equal-source arbitration exposes the error. Separate flags share a destination; slash-paired options remain regression controls.

source_candidate.User Query Draft: A paired `--with-x/--without-x` option ignores an explicitly supplied disabling flag in some default configurations. The explicit flag must always beat the configured default. Fix it without changing the no-argument behavior.
source_candidate.Damage Mutation: Break the tie-break between an explicitly selected flag value and an explicit default so default can overwrite user input.
source_candidate.Failure Symptom: `--without-x` yields the default enabled value; no-argument and `--with-x` may still pass.
source_candidate.Expected SOP: List possible sources including explicit-default metadata → check tie-break after parsing → test all flag combinations.
source_candidate.Key Discovery: A default can itself carry provenance; precedence must be decided after tracking source, not by comparing values.
source_candidate.Grader Assertions: No flag keeps default; each explicit flag wins; paired flags remain deterministic.
source_candidate.Why Skill Helps: This is intentionally a near-neighbor of T01 but at a different tie-break stage, testing whether the Skill generalizes beyond envvars.
